title: Glenn Ellison, MIT 14.271: Lecture 1, Monopoly Pricing and Durable Goods, Part I (Fall 2022)
use: Single-product monopoly profit, MR=MC and the Lerner elasticity condition; conventional deadweight-loss versus profit/consumer-surplus distinction. The chapter supplies its own global and activation comparisons.
verification: Retrieved the actual official 26-page lecture PDF and inspected slides 2–3 for the single-product model, formula and welfare account. The scope does not include adoption or verification of the document's multiproduct, quality, durable-good or information-design extensions. Chapter derivations, data and numerical cases are original; the positive elasticity-magnitude convention is explicitly defined rather than silently copying a signed-elasticity formula.

title: Glenn Ellison, MIT 14.271: Lecture 5, Static Competition and Models of Differentiation, Part 1 (Fall 2022)

title: Glenn Ellison, MIT 14.271: Lecture 16, Entry (Fall 2022)
use: Entry investment versus profits in the subsequent competition model, and the distinction between private entry incentives and the full consumer/producer/fixed-cost welfare account.
verification: Retrieved the actual official 16-page PDF and inspected slides 2–8 on two-stage entry and welfare effects. The chapter uses only the timing and accounting distinctions in an original one-entrant example, with an explicit no-discounting horizon, and independently proves a simple fixed-cost subadditivity comparison. No general excessive-entry theorem, dynamic learning model, current barrier allegation or legal conclusion is imported.
